body: Two separate methods. (A) Special situations (You Can Be a Stock Market Genius): spin-offs (parent holders sell the unwanted child regardless of price; insiders often get equity incentives in the new entity), restructurings, merger securities, rights offerings, recapitalisations and LEAPS. Edge comes from non-economic selling and small size. Indian analogues: demergers (e.g., recent conglomerate splits), open offers and buyback arbitrage, rights issues priced at deep discounts. (B) Magic Formula (2005): rank stocks by return on capital = EBIT / (net working capital + net fixed assets) and earnings yield = EBIT / enterprise value, sum ranks, buy top 20-30, hold one year, repeat; exclude financials/utilities. Backtest 1988-2004: ~30.8%/yr vs ~12.4% for the S&P 500; live results were much weaker, and multi-year underperformance led most users to abandon it - Greenblatt's own point is that it works because it is hard to stick with. Use as an idea generator plus a quality/governance check in India, where cheap high-ROC stocks often include cyclicals at peak margins and promoter-governance risks.
title: Greenblatt: special situations plus Magic Formula screen
